first: चौ॰—चले राम लछिमन मुनि सङ्गा। गये जहाँ जग-पावनि गङ्गा॥
en: Rama and Lakshmana went on with the sage and came to the Ganga, which purifies the world. The son of Gadhi told them the whole story of how the heavenly river came down to earth.

first: तब प्रभु रिषिन्ह समेत नहाये। बिबिध दान महिदेवन्ह पाये।
en: Then the Lord bathed with the sages, and the Brahmins received many kinds of gifts. Gladly they went on with the band of sages and soon drew near the city of Videha.

first: पुर रस्यता राम जब देखी। हरषे अनुज समेत बिसेखी॥
en: When Rama saw the beauty of the city, he and his brother were very glad. There were many step-wells, wells, streams and lakes, with water like nectar and steps made of gems.

first: गुज्जत मज्जु मत्त-रस भृङ्गा। कूजत कल बहु बरन बिहङ्गा॥
en: Bees drunk on honey hummed sweetly, and birds of many colours sang softly. Lotuses of every colour were in bloom, and a cool, gentle, fragrant breeze always gave delight.

first: दो॰—सुमन बाटिका बाग बन, बिपुल विहङ्ग निवास।
en: Flower gardens, orchards and groves, home to many birds, full of flowers, fruit and fresh leaves, adorned the city on every side.

first: चौ॰—बनइ न बरनत नगर निकाई। जहाँ जाइ मन तहइँ लोभाई॥
en: The charm of the city cannot be described; wherever the mind goes, there it is captured. The markets were lovely, and the balconies wonderful, set with gems, as if the Creator had shaped them with his own hands.

first: धनिक-बनिक बर धनद समाना। बैठे सकल बस्तु लेइ नाना॥
en: Rich merchants, each like Kubera the god of wealth, sat with all kinds of goods. The squares and lanes were beautiful and always sprinkled with fragrant water.

first: मङ्गल-मय मन्दिर सब केरे। चित्रित जनु रतिनाथ चितेरे॥
en: Everyone's houses were full of good things, painted as if by Love himself. The men and women of the city were fortunate, pure and saintly, righteous, wise and full of virtue.

first: अति अनूप जहँ जनक-निवासू। विथ कहिँ शिबुध बिलोकि बिलासू॥
en: Where Janaka lived was beyond compare, and the gods were amazed to see its splendour. The mind was struck with wonder at the sight of the fort, as if it held in itself the beauty of all the worlds.

first: दो॰—धवल-धाम मनि-पुरट-पट, सुघटित नाना भाँति।
en: White palaces, with doors of gems and gold, were finely built in many ways. How can one describe the beauty of the lovely house where Sita lived?

first: चो॰—सुभग द्वार सब कुलिस कपाठा। भूप भीर नट मागध भाटा॥
en: All the gates were fine, with doors as strong as thunderbolts, and crowded with kings, dancers, bards and heralds. There were large stables for horses and elephants, always full of horses, elephants and chariots.

first: सूर सचिव सेनप बहुतेरे। नृप गृह सरिस सदन सब केरे॥
en: There were many warriors, ministers and generals, and all their houses were like a king's palace. Outside the city, near lakes and rivers, many kings had made their camps here and there.

first: देखि अनूप एक अँबराई। सव सुपास सब भाँति सुहाई॥
en: Seeing a matchless mango grove, comfortable in every way and lovely, Kaushika said, 'This pleases my heart; wise hero of the Raghus, let us stay here.'

first: भलेहि नाथ कहि कृपा निकेता। उत्तरे तहँ मुनि-वृन्द समेता॥
en: Saying, 'Very well, master,' the home of mercy stopped there with the band of sages. The king of Mithila got the news that the great sage Vishvamitra had come.

first: दो॰—सङ्ग सचिव सुचि भूरि भट, भूसुर बर गुरु ज्ञाति।
en: Taking with him his honest ministers, many warriors, the best Brahmins, his guru and his kin, the king gladly set out to meet the chief of sages.

first: चौ॰—कीन्ह प्रनाम चरन धरि माथा। दीन्हि असीस मुदित मुनिनाथा॥
en: He bowed, laying his head at the sage's feet, and the lord of sages gladly blessed him. He respectfully greeted all the Brahmins, and the king rejoiced, thinking himself very lucky.

first: कुसल प्रस्न कहि बारहिँ बारा। विस्वामित्र नृपहि बैठारा॥
en: After asking again and again about his welfare, Vishvamitra seated the king. Just then the two brothers came back; they had gone to see the gardens.

first: स्याम गौर मृदु बयस किसाेरा। लोचन सुखद बिस्व-चित चाेरा।
en: One dark and one fair, gentle and young, a joy to the eyes, stealing the hearts of all the world. When the Lord of the Raghus came, everyone rose, and Vishvamitra seated them beside him.

first: भये सब सुखी देखि दोउ भ्राता। बारि बिलोचन पुलकित गाता॥
en: Everyone was happy to see the two brothers, with tears in their eyes and bodies thrilling. Seeing their sweet and lovely forms, Videha, the bodiless one, truly forgot his body.

first: दो॰—प्रेम मगन मन जानि नृप, करि बिबेक धरि धीर।
en: Knowing his mind was lost in love, the king used his judgment and steadied himself. Bowing his head at the sage's feet, he spoke in a deep voice choked with feeling.

first: ची॰—कहहुनाथसुन्दरदोउबालक। मुनिकुल-तिलक कि नृपकुल-पालक॥
en: 'Tell me, master, are these two lovely boys the pride of a family of sages or protectors of a royal line? Or has that Brahman whom the Vedas sing as "not this" come in two forms?'

first: सहज बिराग-रूप मन माेरा। थकित होत जिमि चन्द चकोरा॥
en: 'My mind, which is detachment itself by nature, is held still by them, as the chakor bird is by the moon. So, lord, I ask you truly: tell me, master, and hide nothing.'

first: इन्हहिँ बिलोकत अति अनुरागा। बरबस ब्रह्म-सुखहि मन त्यागा॥
en: 'Looking at them with great love, my mind has been forced to give up the bliss of Brahman.' The sage smiled and said, 'King, you have spoken well; your words cannot be false.'

first: ये प्रिय सबहि जहाँ लगि प्रानी। मन मुसुकाहिँ राम सुनि बानी॥
en: 'They are dear to every living being.' Hearing this, Rama smiled inwardly. 'They are sons of Dasharatha, jewel of the Raghu clan, and the king has sent them to help me.'

first: दो॰—राम लखन दोउ बन्धु बर, रूप-सील-बल धाम।
en: 'Rama and Lakshmana, two fine brothers, homes of beauty, good nature and strength, guarded my sacrifice and defeated the demons in battle, as the whole world can witness.'

first: चौ॰—मुनि तव चरन देखि कह राऊ। कहि न सकउँ निज पुन्य प्रभाऊ॥
en: The king said, 'Sage, now that I have seen your feet, I cannot tell how great my merit is. These two lovely brothers, dark and fair, give joy even to joy itself.'

first: इन्ह कै प्रीति परसपर पावनि। कहि न जाइ मन भाव सुहावनि॥
en: 'Their pure love for each other is lovely beyond words and touches the heart.' Glad Videha said, 'Listen, master, their love is natural, like that between Brahman and the soul.'

first: पुनि पुनि प्रभुहि चितव नरनाहू। पुलक गात उर अधिक उछाहू॥
en: Again and again the king gazed at the Lord, his body thrilling and his heart full of delight. Praising the sage and bowing his head at his feet, the king led them into the city.

first: सुन्दर सदन सुखद् सब काला। तहाँ बास लेइ दीन्ह भुआला॥
en: The king gave them lodging in a lovely house, pleasant in every season. After worshipping them and serving them in every way, the king took leave and went home.

first: दो॰—रिषय सङ्घ रघुबंस-मनि, करि भोजन विस्त्राम।
en: The jewel of the Raghu clan ate and rested with the sages, and then sat with his brother; a quarter of the day was still left.

first: चौ॰—लखन हृदय लालसा बिसेखी। जाइ जनकपुर आइय देखी॥
en: Lakshmana had a strong wish in his heart to go and see Janakpur. But in awe of the Lord and shy before the sage, he did not say it aloud, only smiling inwardly.

first: राम अनुज मन की गति जानी। भगतबछलता हिय हुलसानी॥
en: Rama knew what was in his brother's mind, and his love for his devotees welled up. Very humbly and shyly, smiling, he spoke after getting the guru's leave.

first: नाथ लखन पुर देखन चहहीँ। प्रभु सकोच डर प्रकट न कहहीँ॥
en: 'Master, Lakshmana wants to see the city, but out of shyness and fear of you he does not say so. If I have your permission, I will show him the city and bring him back soon.'

first: सुनि मुनीस कह बचन सप्रीती। कस न राम तुम्ह राखहु नीती॥
en: Hearing this, the lord of sages said lovingly, 'Rama, why would you not keep good conduct? Dear son, you are the keeper of the bridge of dharma, moved by love and giving joy to your servants.'

first: दो॰—जाइ देखि आवहु नगर, सुख-निधान दोउ भाइ।
en: 'Go and see the city and come back, you two brothers, treasures of joy. Show your lovely faces and make everyone's eyes fruitful.'

first: चौ॰—मुनि-पद-कमल बन्दि दोउ भ्राता। चले लोक-लोचन सुख-दाता॥
en: Bowing at the sage's lotus feet, the two brothers set out, giving joy to the eyes of the world. Seeing their great beauty, crowds of boys followed them, their eyes and hearts enchanted.

first: पीत-बसन परिकर कटि माथा। चारु चाप सर सेाहत हाथा॥
en: They wore yellow clothes, with sashes at their waists, and lovely bows and arrows shone in their hands. Sandal paste marked their bodies, matching their colour, a charming pair, dark and fair.

first: कैहरि-कन्धर बाहु बिसाला। उर अति रुचिर नाग-मनि-माला॥
en: They had shoulders like a lion's and long arms, and lovely garlands of elephant pearls on their chests. Their lotus eyes were fine and red at the corners, and their moon-like faces took away the three kinds of pain.

first: कानन्हि कनक-फूल छबि देहीँ। चितवत चितहि चोरि जनु लेहीँ॥
en: Golden flowers in their ears added beauty, and their glances seemed to steal the heart. Their gaze was lovely, their brows finely curved, and the mark on their foreheads seemed to seal their beauty.

first: दो॰—रुचिर चौतनी सुभग सिर, मेचक कुञ्चित केस।
en: Lovely square caps sat on their fine heads, over dark curly hair. The two brothers were beautiful from head to toe, every part perfectly formed.

first: चौ॰—देखन नगर भूप-सुत आये। समाचार पुरबासिन्ह पाये॥
en: The people of the city heard that the king's sons had come to see the city. They ran out, leaving their homes and work, like beggars rushing to loot a treasure.

first: निरखि सहज सुन्दर दोउ भाई। होहिँ सुखी लोचन फल पाई॥
en: Gazing at the two naturally beautiful brothers, they were happy, their eyes rewarded. Young women at the windows of their houses gazed lovingly at Rama's form.

first: कहहिँ परसपर बचन सप्रीती। सखि इन्ह कोटि काम छबि जीती॥
en: They said to one another fondly, 'Friend, they have beaten the beauty of millions of Love gods. Among gods, men, demons, Nagas and sages, one never hears of such beauty.'

first: बिष्नु चारि भुज बिधि मुख चारी। बिकट-बेष मुख-पञ्च पुरारी॥
en: 'Vishnu has four arms, Brahma four faces, and Shiva, enemy of the three cities, five faces and a fearsome look. Friend, there is no other god whose beauty could be compared with this.'

first: दो॰—बय किसोर सुखमा-सदन, स्याम गौर सुख-धाम।
en: 'Young in age, homes of grace, one dark and one fair, abodes of joy: on every limb of theirs one could offer up billions of Love gods.'

first: चौ॰—कहहु सखी अस को तनुधारी। जो न मोह यह रूप निहारी॥
en: 'Tell me, friend, what living being would not be charmed on seeing this form?' One woman spoke softly with love, 'Listen, wise one, to what I have heard.'

first: ये दोऊ दसरथ के ढाेटा। बाल-मरालन्ह के कल जोटा।
en: 'These two are Dasharatha's sons, a lovely pair like young swans. They guarded the sage Kaushika's sacrifice and killed the demons on the battlefield.'

first: स्याम-गात कल-कञ्ज-बिलोचन। जो मारीच-सुभुज-मद मोचन॥
en: 'The one with the dark body and lovely lotus eyes, who broke the pride of Maricha and Subahu, is Kausalya's son, a mine of joy; his name is Rama, and he holds bow and arrows.'

first: गौर किसोर बेष बर काछे। कर-सर-चाप राम के पाछे।
en: 'The fair youth, finely dressed, with bow and arrows in hand, walking behind Rama, is Lakshmana, Rama's younger brother; listen, friend, his mother is Sumitra.'

first: दो॰—बिप्र काज करि बन्धु दोउ, मग मुनि-बधू उधारि।
en: 'The two brothers did the Brahmin's work, freed the sage's wife on the way, and have come to see the bow sacrifice.' Hearing this, all the women were glad.

first: चौ॰—देखि राम छबि कोउ एक कहई। जोग जानकिहि यह बर अहई।
en: Seeing Rama's beauty, one said, 'This is the right husband for Janaki. Friend, if the king saw him, he would drop his vow and insist on this marriage.'

first: कोउ कह ये भूपति पहिचाने। मुनि समेत सादर सनमाने॥
en: Another said, 'The king has learned who they are and has honoured them with the sage. But friend, the king will not give up his vow; under fate, he clings to his folly.'

first: कोउ कह जाँ भल अहइ बिधाता। सब कहँ सुनिय उचित फलदाता॥
en: Another said, 'If the Creator is good, and gives each the fruit they deserve, as we hear, then Janaki will get this husband; friend, there is no doubt of it.'

first: जौँ बिधि-बस अस बनइ सँजोगू। तौ कृतकृत्य होहिँ सब लोगू॥
en: 'If by fate such a match comes about, all the people will feel their life fulfilled. Friend, that is why I long so much for it, for then they may come here now and then through this tie.'

first: दो॰—नाहिँ त हम कहँ सुनहु सखि, इन्ह कर दरसन दूरि।
en: 'Otherwise, friend, for us the sight of them is far away. Such a meeting happens only when one has a great store of past merit.'

first: चौ॰—बोली अपर कहेहु सखि नीका। एहि बिबाह अति हित सबही का॥
en: Another said, 'Friend, you have spoken well; this marriage would be good for everyone.' Someone said, 'Shankar's bow is very hard, and this dark youth is soft of body.'

first: सब असमञ्जस अहइ सयानी। यह सुनि अपर कहइ मृदु बानी॥
en: 'Wise one, it is all very doubtful.' Hearing this, another said gently, 'Friend, some people say of them that they look small but are mighty.'

first: परसि जासु पद-पङ्कज धूरी। तरी अहिल्या कृत-अघ-भूरी॥
en: 'Ahalya, who had done great wrong, was saved by touching the dust of his lotus feet. Will he rest without breaking Shiva's bow? Do not drop this faith even by mistake.'

first: जेहि बिरज्चि रचि सीय सँवारी। तेहि स्यामल बर रचेउ बिचारी॥
en: 'The Creator who made Sita with such care has thoughtfully made this dark bridegroom for her.' Hearing her words, all were glad and said softly, 'May it be so.'

first: दो॰—हिय हरषहिँ बरषहिँ सुमन, सुमुखि सुलोचनि-वृन्द।
en: Glad at heart, the lovely-faced, bright-eyed women showered flowers. Wherever the two brothers went, there was supreme joy.

first: चौ॰—पुर पूरब-दिसि गे दोउ भाई। जहँ धनु-मख हित भूमि बनाई॥
en: The two brothers went to the east of the city, where ground had been prepared for the bow sacrifice. It was very wide, with a fine paved floor and a clean, lovely altar.

first: चहुँ दिसि कञ्चन मञ्च बिसाला। रचे जहाँ बैठहिँ महिपाला॥
en: On every side were large golden platforms, built for the kings to sit on. Behind them, close by, all around, was a fine ring of other platforms.

first: कछुक ऊँचि सब भाँति सुहाई। बैठहिँ नगर लोग जहँ जाई॥
en: These were somewhat higher and lovely in every way, where the people of the city would go and sit. Near them were large, fine white buildings painted in many colours.

first: जहँ बैठे देखहिँ सब नारी। जथाजोग निज-कुल अनुहारी॥
en: From there all the women would watch, each seated as fit her family's rank. The boys of the city, chattering sweetly, respectfully showed the Lord the arrangements.

first: दो॰—सब सिसु एहि मिस प्रेम-बस, परसि मनोहर गात।
en: With this excuse, out of love, the boys all touched his lovely body; their bodies thrilled and their hearts were full of joy as they gazed at the two brothers.

first: चौ॰—सिसु सब राम प्रेम बस जाने। प्रीति समेत निकेत बखोने॥
en: Rama saw that all the boys were won by love, and he praised the places with affection. Each boy called them as he liked, and the two brothers went with love.

first: राम देखावहिँ अनुजहि रचना। कहि मृदु मधुर मनोहर बचना॥
en: Rama showed the arrangements to his brother, speaking soft, sweet, charming words. He at whose command Maya creates whole worlds in the blink of an eye,

first: भगति हेतु सोइ दीनदयाला। चितवत चकित धनुष-मख-साला॥
en: that same Lord, kind to the humble, out of love for his devotees, looked at the hall of the bow sacrifice with wonder. Having seen the sight, they went back to the guru, afraid at heart that they were late.

first: जासु त्रास डर कहँ डर हाेई। भजन प्रभाव देखावत साेई॥
en: He whose fear makes even fear afraid shows the power of devotion. With soft, sweet, pleasant words he sent the boys away against their will.

first: दो॰—समय सप्रेम बिनीत अति, सकुच सहित दोउ भाइ।
en: Respectful, loving and very humble, the two brothers shyly bowed their heads at the guru's lotus feet and sat down when he told them to.

first: चौ॰—निसि प्रबेस मुनि आयसु दीन्हा। सबही सन्ध्या-बदन कीन्हा॥
en: As night fell, the sage gave the word, and everyone said the evening prayers. Telling old stories and histories, two watches of the lovely night passed.

first: मुनिबर सयन कीन्ह तब जाई। लगे चरन चाँपन दोउ भाई॥
en: Then the great sage went to rest, and the two brothers began to press his feet. For the sake of their lotus feet, ascetics practise many kinds of prayer and yoga,

first: ते दोउ बन्धु प्रेम जनु जीते। गुरु-पद-पदुम पलोटत प्रीते॥
en: yet those two brothers, as if conquered by love, lovingly massaged the guru's lotus feet. Only when the sage told him again and again did the best of the Raghus go to rest.

first: चाँपत चरन लखन उर लाये। समय सप्रेम परम सचु पाये॥
en: Lakshmana pressed Rama's feet, holding them to his heart with awe and love, and found deep peace. Again and again the Lord said, 'Sleep, dear brother,' and Lakshmana lay down holding the lotus feet to his heart.

first: दो॰—उठे लखन निसि बिगत सुनि, अरुनसिखा धुनि कान।
en: Hearing the cock crow and knowing the night was over, Lakshmana rose. Wise Rama, the lord of the world, woke even before the guru.

first: चौ॰—सकल सौच करि जाइ नहाये। नित्य निबाहि मुनिहि सिर नाये॥
en: They washed, went and bathed, finished their daily rites and bowed to the sage. Knowing it was time, with the guru's leave, the two brothers went to gather flowers.

first: भूप बाग बर देखेउ जाई। जहँ बसन्त-रितु रही लाेभाई॥
en: They went and saw the king's fine garden, where spring itself seemed to have stayed, charmed. Many lovely trees grew there, with canopies of fine creepers of every colour.

first: नव-पल्लव फल सुमन सुहाये। निज-सम्पत्ति सुर-रूख लजाये॥
en: Fresh leaves, fruit and flowers were so lovely that they put the wish-granting trees of heaven to shame with their wealth. Chatak birds, cuckoos, parrots and chakors sang, and peacocks danced gracefully.

first: मध्य बाग सर साह सुहावा। मनि-सोपान बिचित्र बनावा॥
en: In the middle of the garden was a lovely lake, with wonderful steps made of gems. Its water was clear, with lotuses of many colours, water birds calling and bees humming.

first: दो॰—बाग तड़ाग विलोकि प्रक्षु, हरषे बन्धु समेत।
en: Seeing the garden and lake, the Lord and his brother were glad. Most delightful is this garden that gives joy even to Rama.

first: चौ॰—चहुँ दिसि चित्तइ पूछि माली गन। लगे लेन दल फूल मुदित मन॥
en: Looking all around and asking the gardeners, they gladly began to pick leaves and flowers. Just then Sita came there, sent by her mother to worship Girija.

first: सङ्ग सखी सब सुभग सयानी। गावहिँ गीत मनोहर बानी॥
en: With her came all her lovely, clever friends, singing songs in charming voices. Near the lake stood Girija's temple, beautiful beyond words, charming the mind of all who saw it.

first: मज्जन करि सर सखिन्ह समेता। गई मुदित मन गौरि निकेता॥
en: After bathing in the lake with her friends, Sita gladly went to Gauri's temple. She worshipped with great love and asked for a fine husband worthy of her.

first: एक सखी सिय सङ्ग बिहाई। गई रही देखन फुलवाई॥
en: One friend had left Sita's side and gone to see the garden. She saw the two brothers and came back to Sita, overcome with love.

first: दो॰—तासु दसा देखी सखिन्ह, पुलक-गात जल-नैन।
en: Her friends saw her state, her body thrilling and her eyes wet. They all asked gently, 'Tell us the reason for your joy.'

first: चौ॰—देखन बाग कुँअर दुइ आये। बय-किसोर सब भाँति सुहाये॥
en: 'Two princes have come to see the garden, young and lovely in every way, one dark and one fair. How can I describe them? Speech has no eyes, and the eyes have no speech.'

first: सुनि हरषीँ सब सखी सयानी। सिय हिय अति उतकंठा जानी॥
en: Hearing this, all the clever friends were glad, for they knew how eager Sita was at heart. One said, 'Friend, they must be the king's sons we heard came with the sage yesterday,'

first: जिन्ह निज रूप मोहनी डारी। कान्हे स्वबस नगर-नर-नारी॥
en: 'who have cast the spell of their beauty and won over the men and women of the city. Everyone everywhere is praising their beauty; we must surely see them, for they are worth seeing.'

first: तासु अचन अति सियहि सुहाने। दरस लागि लोचन अकुलाने॥
en: Her words pleased Sita greatly, and her eyes grew restless to see him. Putting that dear friend in front, she went; no one knew her love was an old one.

first: दो॰—सुमिरि सीय नारद बचन, उपजी प्राति पुनीत।
en: Remembering Narada's words, Sita felt a holy love rise in her. She looked about in every direction, startled, like a frightened young doe.

first: चौ॰—कङ्कन किङ्किनि नूपुर धुनि सुनि। कहत लखन सन राम हृदय गुनि॥
en: Hearing the jingle of bangles, waist bells and anklets, Rama thought in his heart and said to Lakshmana, 'It is as if Love has beaten his war drum, set on conquering the world.'

first: अस कहि फिरि चितये तेहि ओरा। सिय मुख ससि भये नयन चकोरा।
en: Saying this, he turned and looked that way, and his eyes became chakor birds to the moon of Sita's face. His lovely eyes grew still, as if Nimi, out of shyness, had left the eyelids.

first: देखि सीय सोभा सुख पावा। हृदय सराहत बचन न आवा॥
en: Seeing Sita's beauty he felt joy; he praised her in his heart but could not speak. It was as if the Creator had put all his skill into her and shown it to the world.

first: सुन्दरता कहँ सुन्दर करई। छबि-गृह दीप-सिखा जनु बरई॥
en: She makes beauty itself beautiful, like a lamp flame burning in a house of beauty. Poets have used up all comparisons; with what can I compare the daughter of Videha?

first: दो॰—सिय सोभा हिय बरनि प्रभु, आपनि दसा बिचारि।
en: Describing Sita's beauty in his heart and thinking of his own state, the Lord, pure in mind, spoke to his brother as the moment called for.

first: चौ॰—तात जनक तनया यह साेई। धनुष-यज्ञ जेहि कापुन हाेई॥
en: 'Brother, this is Janaka's daughter, for whom the bow sacrifice is being held. Her friends have brought her to worship Gauri, and she moves through the garden, lighting it up.'

first: जासु बिलोकि अलौकिक सोभा। सहज पुनीत माेर मन छोमा॥
en: 'Seeing her unearthly beauty, my mind, pure by nature, is stirred. The Creator alone knows the reason, but listen, brother, my good-luck limbs are throbbing.'

first: रघुवंसिन्ह कर सहज सुभाऊ। भन कुपन्थ पग घरइँ न कऊ॥
en: 'It is the nature of the Raghu line that their minds never step onto a wrong path. I have full faith in my mind, which has never looked at another man's wife even in a dream.'

first: जिन्ह कै लहहिँ न रिपु रन पीठी। नहिँ पावहिँ परतिय मन दीठी॥
en: 'Those whose backs enemies never see in battle, who never give their heart or glance to another's wife, and from whom beggars never hear no: such fine men are few in the world.'

first: दो॰—करत बतकही अनुज सन, मन सिय रूप लोभान।
en: While talking with his brother, his mind was drawn to Sita's beauty, and like a bee he drank the nectar of the beauty of her lotus face.

first: चौ॰—चितवति चकित चहूँदिसि सीता। कहँ गये नृप-किसोर मन चिन्ता॥
en: Sita looked all around in wonder, worried: 'Where have the princes gone?' Wherever the fawn-eyed one looked, it was as if a row of white lotuses rained there.

first: लता ओट तब सखिन्ह लखाये। स्यामल गौर किसोर सुहाये॥
en: Then her friends pointed them out behind a screen of creepers, the lovely young pair, dark and fair. Seeing his form her eyes were filled with longing, glad as if they had found their own lost treasure.

first: थके नयन रघुपति छबि देखे। पलकन्हिहूँ परिहरी निमेखे॥
en: Her eyes stood still at the sight of Rama's beauty, and even her eyelids stopped blinking. In her great love she forgot her body, like a chakor bird gazing at the autumn moon.

first: लोचन मग रामहिँ उर आनी। दीन्हे पलक कपाट सयानी॥
en: Bringing Rama into her heart by the path of her eyes, the wise one closed the doors of her eyelids. When her friends saw Sita lost in love, they felt shy and could say nothing.

first: दो॰—लता-भवन से प्रगट भे, तेहि अवसर दोउ भाइ।
en: Just then the two brothers came out from the bower of creepers, like two bright moons coming out from a bank of clouds.

first: चौ॰—सोभा सीँव सुभग दोउ बीरा। नील-पीत-जलजात सरीरा॥
en: The two fine heroes were the limit of beauty, their bodies like blue and yellow lotuses. Peacock feathers shone on their heads, with clusters of flower buds among them.

first: भाल तिलक स्त्रम-बिन्दु सुहाये। स्त्रवन सुभग भूषन छबि छाये॥
en: Marks on their foreheads and drops of sweat looked lovely, and fine ornaments shone in their ears. Their brows were curved, their hair curly, and their eyes red at the corners like fresh lotuses.

first: चारु चिबुक नासिका कपोला। हास बिलास लेत मन मोला॥
en: Lovely chins, noses and cheeks, and their playful smiles bought the heart. I cannot describe the beauty of their faces, which would put many Love gods to shame.

first: उर-मनि-माल कम्बु कल ग्रीवाँ। काम-कलम-कर भुज बल सीवाँ॥
en: A necklace of gems on the chest, a lovely neck like a conch, arms like a young elephant's trunk, the limit of strength; in his left hand a leaf cup of flowers: friend, the dark prince is very handsome.

first: दो॰—केहरि-कटि पट-पीत-धर, सुखमा-सीलनिधान।
en: With a lion's waist, wearing yellow cloth, a treasure of grace and good nature: seeing the ornament of the Sun dynasty, the friends forgot themselves.

first: चौ॰—धरि धीरज,एक आलि सयानी। सीता सन बाली गहि पानी॥
en: Taking courage, one clever friend took Sita's hand and said, 'You can meditate on Gauri later; why not look at the prince now?'

first: सकुचि सीय तब नयन उधारे। सनमुख दोउ रघु सिंह निहारे॥
en: Shyly Sita then opened her eyes and saw the two lions of the Raghus before her. Seeing Rama's beauty from head to toe and remembering her father's vow, her mind was greatly troubled.

first: परबस सखिन्ह लखी जब सीता। मयउ गहरु सब कहहिँ सभीता॥
en: When her friends saw that Sita was no longer her own, they all said anxiously, 'It is getting late.' One friend, smiling inwardly, said, 'We will come again at this time tomorrow.'

first: गूढ़गिरा सुनि सिय सकुचानी। मयउ बिलम्ब मातु भय मानी॥
en: Hearing these veiled words, Sita felt shy; afraid of her mother because it was late, she took great courage, holding Rama in her heart, and turned back, knowing herself to be in her father's hands.

first: दो॰—देखन मिस मृग बिहँग तरु, फिरइ बहोरि बहाेरि।
en: Pretending to look at deer, birds and trees, she turned again and again; each time she saw the beauty of the hero of the Raghus, her love grew greatly.

first: चौ॰—जानि,कठिन सिव चाप बिसूरति। चली राखि उर स्यामल मूरति॥
en: Knowing that Shiva's bow was hard, she grieved, and went away holding the dark form in her heart. When the Lord knew that Janaki was leaving, that mine of joy, love, beauty and virtue,

first: परमप्रेममय मृदु मसि कीन्ही। चारु चित्र भीतर लिखि लीन्ही॥
en: he made ink of supreme love and drew her lovely picture inside his heart. Sita went again to Bhavani's temple, bowed at her feet and spoke with joined hands.

first: जय जय गिरि-बर-राज किसोरी। जय महेस-मुख-चन्द चकोरी॥
en: 'Glory, glory to the daughter of the king of mountains! Glory to you, chakor bird to the moon of Mahesh's face! Glory to the mother of the elephant-faced one and the six-faced one, mother of the world, whose body shines like lightning!'

first: नहिँ तव आदि मध्य अवसाना। अमित प्रभाव बेद नहिँ जाना॥
en: 'You have no beginning, middle or end; even the Vedas do not know your boundless power. You cause the birth, life and end of the world; you charm the universe and move freely by your own will.'

first: दो॰—पतिदेवता सुतीय महँ, मातु प्रथम तव रेख।
en: 'Mother, among good wives who worship their husbands as gods, you come first. Your glory is boundless; even a thousand Sharadas and Sheshas cannot tell it.'

first: चौ॰—सेवत ताेहि सुलभ फल चारी। बर-दायिनि त्रिपुरारि पियारी॥
en: 'By serving you, the four goals of life are easily won, giver of boons, beloved of the enemy of the three cities. Goddess, by worshipping your lotus feet, all gods, men and sages become happy.'

first: मोर मनोरथ जानहु नीके। बसहु सदा उर-पुर सबही के॥
en: 'You know my wish well, for you always live in the city of everyone's heart. That is why I have not said it aloud.' Saying this, Vaidehi clasped her feet.

first: बिनय प्रेम-बस भई भवानी। खसी माल मूरति मुसुकानी॥
en: Bhavani was moved by her humble love; her garland slipped down and the image smiled. Sita respectfully placed the blessed gift on her head, and Gauri spoke, her heart full of joy.

first: सुनु सिय सत्य असीस हमारी। पूजिहि मन-कामना तुम्हारी॥
en: 'Listen, Sita, my blessing is true: your heart's wish will be fulfilled. Narada's words are always pure and true; you will get the husband your heart is set on.'

first: मन जाहि राचेउ मिलिहि सो बर- सहज सुन्दर साँवरो।
en: 'You will get the husband your heart is set on, the naturally handsome dark one; he is a treasure of mercy and all-knowing, and knows your goodness and love.' Hearing Gauri's blessing, Sita and her friends were glad at heart; says Tulsi, she worshipped Bhavani again and again and went back to the palace with a happy mind.

first: सो॰—जानि गौरि अनुकूल, सिय-हिय-हरष न जाइ कहि।
en: Knowing Gauri was pleased with her, Sita felt a joy beyond words, and her left limbs, the lovely root of good fortune, began to throb.
